title: Trinity Sunday
hookLine: the one Sunday for the mystery at the heart of it all

lines: THE SEA IN A HOLE IN THE SAND.
cards: A legend is told about Augustine, the North African bishop and writer. He's walking a beach, turning over a hard question: how can God be one, and also three?
He finds a child running to the sea with a shell, pouring water into a little hole in the sand. What are you doing? Putting the sea in this hole.
Augustine laughs: that's impossible. And the child answers, more or less, so is fitting God into your head. The legend doesn't need to be true to land.
After Easter and Pentecost, the calendar keeps one Sunday just for that question. Today, Trinity Sunday.

teach.h: THE LORD OUR GOD IS ONE LORD.
teach.b: Start with one God. Moses says it in Deuteronomy, in the King James Bible: "Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD." Jesus quotes it himself when asked which commandment comes first.
And yet the Gospels keep naming three together. At Jesus's baptism in Matthew, the Spirit comes down like a dove, and a voice from heaven says, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."

teach.h: FATHER, SON AND SPIRIT IN ONE SCENE.
teach.b: Father speaking, Son in the water, Spirit descending, in one scene. At the end of Matthew, Jesus sends his friends out "baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost."

teach.h: IN THE NAME, NOT THE NAMES.
teach.b: Some Christian readers point out: the name, not the names. And Paul signs off a letter: "The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all."
Over time the church found a word for what these texts hold together: Trinity. One God, say Christians who hold the creeds, in three persons. Not three gods.
Not one God wearing three masks. Father, Son and Spirit, each fully God, and one. Some teachers say every picture falls short: shamrocks, water and ice and steam help a little, then leak.

That's why Christians call it a mystery: not a puzzle awaiting a clever answer, but something held true that you can live inside without reaching the bottom. The sea doesn't fit in the hole. People still swim in it.

how: On Trinity Sunday some churches sing hymns to the Trinity and say a creed, and preachers often take up the texts where Father, Son and Spirit are named together.

s: Christians who hold the creeds believe in three gods
they say one God, in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
in Matthew's baptism scene, Father, Son and Spirit all appear
the Son in the water, the Spirit like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven.
in Christian use, a mystery is a puzzle waiting to be solved
it's something held to be true that you can live inside without getting to the bottom of it.

games.q: you're on the beach. a child is pouring the sea into a hole with a shell. you say it's impossible. what does the child say back?
o: "so is fitting God into your head."
"the tide will do it for me."
games.why: in the legend told about Augustine, the child says, more or less, that understanding God fully is just as impossible.

practice: Bring to mind something you know is true but can't fully explain: the way a parent loves three children completely, or what a person is, really, behind the face.
If you pray, rest in Paul's farewell, the grace of Christ, the love of God, the communion of the Spirit; if you don't, let the big thing stay big, and sit beside it.

wordCard.voice: Trinity Sunday. The Sunday after Pentecost, for the Christian belief in one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit: in Christian words, a mystery, not a puzzle.

carryVoice: Your line: three in one. Some things are for living inside, not for solving. Back tomorrow, same hill.
